outcome: As of 13 Oct 2026 the classical Littlewood conjecture (liminf of n‖nα‖‖nβ‖ = 0 for every real pair) is still open; no event since 26 Jan 2024 settles it or a case of it. In-window activity is on the uniform variant (disproved by Schleischitz, 13 Mar 2026, and extended by four further preprints through 25 Aug 2026, one of which credits GPT-5.6 Pro with help on calculations and proof-checking), on p-adic and function-field analogues, and on a divisibility-restricted variant; the one in-window event touching the named quantity m_LC is a 2026 numerical bound that I could not locate.
problem_asks: (a) For every pair of real numbers α and β, not only almost every pair or a restricted class of pairs. (b) The quantity liminf as n tends to infinity of n·‖nα‖·‖nβ‖, where n runs over positive integers and ‖x‖ is the distance from x to the nearest integer; homogeneous, so no shifts. (c) The assertion that this liminf equals 0. The inequality ≥ 0 is trivial, so the content is that the product is arbitrarily small for infinitely many n. (d) Only the two-number real case is asked: not the p-adic, function-field, uniform, inhomogeneous or n-number versions. Wikipedia's lead and the constant-m_LC formulation (sup over pairs of inf over n of n‖nα‖‖nβ‖, equal to 0 if and only if the conjecture holds, per the article's numerical section) give the same statement.

events.what_happened: Cassels and Swinnerton-Dyer, ‘On the product of three homogeneous linear forms and the indefinite ternary quadratic forms’, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A (1955), proved the conjecture for every pair (α, β) for which 1, α, β span a totally real cubic number field. Taken from the Wikipedia article and its reference list; the original paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Settles the conjecture for the class of pairs whose three numbers 1, α, β span a totally real cubic field. Restriction: that algebraic-field class only.
events.remains: Every pair outside the totally real cubic class, i.e. the general case.

checked_by.who: J. W. S. Cassels and H. P. F. Swinnerton-Dyer
checked_by.qualification: The authors; the paper appeared in a refereed journal of record.
checked_by.what_they_did: Proof published in Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A.

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture on the cubic-field class.

events.what_happened: Gallagher, ‘Metric simultaneous Diophantine approximation’, J. London Math. Soc. (1962), showed that for almost every pair (α, β) the liminf of n(log n)²‖nα‖‖nβ‖ is 0. Taken from the Wikipedia article; the original was not opened.
events.delivers: Almost every pair (Lebesgue measure): the conjecture holds in a stronger, log²-weighted form. Restriction: a full-measure set of pairs.
events.remains: The pairs in the Lebesgue-null exceptional set, i.e. the conjecture for every pair.

checked_by.qualification: The author; refereed journal of record.
checked_by.what_they_did: Proof published in J. London Math. Soc.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Pollington and Velani, ‘On a problem in simultaneous Diophantine approximation: Littlewood’s conjecture’, Acta Math. 185 (2000) 287–306. Per a search summary and the Wikipedia reference list: for each badly approximable α there is a subset A(α) of the badly approximable numbers, of Hausdorff dimension 1, such that for every β in A(α) the conjecture holds for (α, β). The paper is paywalled and was not opened; the search summary also remarks that the method cannot prove the conjecture by looking only at convergents.
events.delivers: For a given badly approximable α, the conjecture holds for all β in a dimension-one subset of the badly approximable numbers. Restriction: both coordinates badly approximable, and β confined to A(α).
events.remains: Pairs (α, β) with both badly approximable and β outside A(α). Pairs with a non-badly-approximable coordinate are already covered by the trivial case.

checked_by.qualification: The authors; refereed journal of record.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Adamczewski and Bugeaud, ‘On the Littlewood conjecture in simultaneous Diophantine approximation’, arXiv math/0511678 (v1 28 Nov 2005), J. London Math. Soc. 73 (2006) 355–366. For any real α with bounded partial quotients, they construct explicitly continuum many β with bounded partial quotients for which (α, β) satisfies ‘a strong form of the Littlewood conjecture’, by an elementary continued-fraction argument.
events.revisions: v1 28 Nov 2005; published J. London Math. Soc. (2006).
events.delivers: For every fixed α with bounded partial quotients, continuum many explicitly constructed β with bounded partial quotients satisfy the ‘strong form’. Restriction: bounded-type α, and β from the constructed family. The abstract I read does not define the ‘strong form’; the later pass should check whether it is the bare liminf-zero statement or a stronger one.
events.remains: Bounded-type α with β outside the constructed family; all other pairs.

checked_by.qualification: The authors; refereed journal of record.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published in J. London Math. Soc.

events.directly_checkable: The constructed β are explicit; the check is by continued-fraction computation.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; supports it on a class of pairs.
events.object: Explicit continuum-many β with bounded partial quotients attached to any fixed bounded-type α; the pair satisfies the ‘strong form’ (abstract wording; definition not read). Constructive.

events.what_happened: Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss, ‘Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood’s conjecture’, arXiv math/0612721 (v1 22 Dec 2006), Ann. of Math. 164 (2006) 513–560. Abstract: ‘We apply this to prove that the set of exceptions to Littlewood’s conjecture has Hausdorff dimension zero.’ Venkatesh’s 2008 Bull. AMS exposition digests the argument (search link only, not opened).
events.revisions: v1 22 Dec 2006; published Ann. of Math. (2006).
events.delivers: The set of pairs (α, β) violating the conjecture has Hausdorff dimension zero. Restriction: a dimension statement only; the abstract does not claim the set is empty. Venkatesh’s exposition is secondary.
events.remains: Whether the exceptional set is empty, i.e. the conjecture itself.

checked_by.who: Manfred Einsiedler, Anatole Katok, Elon Lindenstrauss
checked_by.qualification: The authors; refereed journal of record (Annals of Mathematics).
Expert in homogeneous dynamics and Diophantine approximation.
checked_by.what_they_did: Expository article digesting the EKL argument in the Bull. AMS (2008).

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: any counterexamples form a dimension-zero set.

events.what_happened: Shapira, ‘A solution to a problem of Cassels and Diophantine properties of cubic numbers’, Ann. of Math. (2011). Per the Wikipedia article, a stronger inhomogeneous version of the cubic-field result. Known from the Wikipedia text and reference list only; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: A stronger, shifted (inhomogeneous) statement for the pairs covered by the Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer cubic-field result. Restriction: that cubic class, and the inhomogeneous form.
events.remains: The homogeneous conjecture for pairs outside the cubic class.

checked_by.qualification: The author; refereed journal of record.

events.doubts: Not opened; the description rests on the Wikipedia sentence alone.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Bugeaud and Moshchevitin, ‘Badly approximable numbers and Littlewood-type problems’, arXiv 0905.0830 (ID indicates May 2009), Math. Proc. Cambridge Phil. Soc. (2011). Per the Wikipedia article: there exist pairs with liminf n(log n)²‖nα‖‖nβ‖ > 0. Not opened.
events.delivers: Existence of pairs for which the log²-weighted liminf is positive. This is a weighted variant; the unweighted conjecture is not affected.
events.remains: The unweighted conjecture for all pairs.

checked_by.qualification: The authors; refereed journal of record.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published in Math. Proc. Cambridge Phil. Soc.

events.doubts: Not opened; the month comes from the arXiv identifier, and the description from the Wikipedia article.
events.direction: Cuts against the log²-weighted variant only; no bearing on the unweighted statement.

events.what_happened: Badziahin, ‘On multiplicatively badly approximable numbers’, arXiv 1101.1855 (v1 10 Jan 2011), Mathematika. Abstract: with an extra factor log q·log log q the statement ‘is false’; the set of (x, y) with liminf q·log q·log log q·‖qx‖‖qy‖ > 0 is of full dimension.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jan 2011; journal version in Mathematika (year given as 2012 on the arXiv page and 2013 in the Wikipedia table).
events.delivers: A full-dimensional set of real pairs for which the log·loglog-weighted Littlewood product stays bounded away from zero. Restriction: the weighted quantity only.
events.remains: The unweighted conjecture; the weight is essential to the result.
events.direction: Cuts against the log·loglog-weighted variant only.

events.what_happened: Badziahin, ‘Computation of the infimum in the Littlewood conjecture’, Experimental Mathematics 25(1) (2016) 100–105, online 12 Oct 2015. Gives an algorithm that certifies m_LC < ε and proves m_LC < 1/19, where m_LC is the supremum over pairs of inf over n of n‖nα‖‖nβ‖; a 2-adic analogue is at most 1/9. A March 2015 accepted version is in the Durham repository. Known from a search summary and the Durham record; not opened.
events.revisions: Durham accepted manuscript dated March 2015; journal online 12 Oct 2015; print 2016.
events.delivers: Upper bound m_LC < 1/19. This bounds the supremum that the conjecture says is 0, so it moves the named quantity without reaching 0. Restriction: a numerical certificate for this constant.
events.remains: m_LC = 0, i.e. the conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: The author; refereed journal of record.

events.directly_checkable: The bound is a computer-certified inequality; the algorithm is in the paper (not read).
events.doubts: Not opened; the figures come from a search summary of the Durham record.
events.direction: Upper bound on the constant that the conjecture equates with zero; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Fregoli and Kleinbock, ‘On multiplicatively badly approximable vectors’, arXiv 2211.04523 (v1 8 Nov 2022; v2 17 Oct 2023; v3 17 Jan 2024; v4 3 Apr 2025). Extends Badziahin’s weighted failure to vectors in R^d with factor (log q)^(d−1)·log log q, and gives a new proof for d = 2 via a new Dani correspondence. Wikipedia lists the paper as J. Number Theory (2026); not verified at the journal.
events.revisions: v1 8 Nov 2022; v2 17 Oct 2023; v3 17 Jan 2024; v4 3 Apr 2025; journal version listed as J. Number Theory (2026) in the Wikipedia reference list.
events.delivers: Weighted failure for the (log q)^(d−1)·log log q-weighted product in R^d, for all d ≥ 2. Restriction: the weighted quantity only.
events.remains: The unweighted d-dimensional statement, and for d = 2 the unweighted classical conjecture.
events.direction: Cuts against the weighted variant in every dimension; no bearing on the unweighted statement.

events.what_happened: Chow and Yang, ‘Effective equidistribution for multiplicative Diophantine approximation on lines’, arXiv 1902.06081 (v1 16 Feb 2019; v2 2 Dec 2023), Invent. Math. (2024, per a search-listed newsletter). For any line in the plane, the conjecture is strengthened by two logarithms for almost every point of the line. Not opened.
events.revisions: v1 16 Feb 2019; v2 2 Dec 2023; journal listed as Invent. Math. (2024) by a secondary source.
events.delivers: A two-logarithm strengthened statement for almost every point on any given line in R². Restriction: a measure-zero-complement set on a line, not all pairs.
events.remains: All pairs off that almost-everywhere set on a line, and all pairs in the plane.
events.doubts: Not opened; the journal listing comes from a search-listed secondary source.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on almost every point of a line.

events.what_happened: Chow and Zafeiropoulos, ‘Fully inhomogeneous multiplicative Diophantine approximation of badly approximable numbers’, arXiv 2103.03605 (2021), Mathematika. Per a search summary: a fully inhomogeneous result for a full-dimensional set of pairs of badly approximable numbers on a vertical line. Not opened.
events.delivers: An inhomogeneous (shifted) statement for a full-dimensional set of badly approximable pairs on a vertical line. Restriction: the shifted form and the set.
events.remains: The homogeneous statement for pairs outside that set; whether the homogeneous case is covered was not checked.
events.doubts: Not opened; scope taken from a search summary.
events.direction: Inhomogeneous variant; no direct bearing on the homogeneous conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chow and Technau, ‘Dispersion and Littlewood’s conjecture’, arXiv 2307.14871 (v1 27 Jul 2023), Adv. Math. 447 (2024). Constructs an explicit full-measure set of α such that for any γ, δ and almost every β there are infinitely many n with n‖nα − γ‖‖nβ − δ‖ < (log log n)^(3+ε)/log n.
events.revisions: v1 27 Jul 2023; published Adv. Math. 447 (2024) per a search summary.
events.delivers: For an explicit full-measure set of α and almost every β, the product is small infinitely often at rate (log log n)^(3+ε)/log n, for any shifts. With γ = δ = 0 this gives liminf zero for that measure-theoretic class of pairs. Restriction: the paper is framed inhomogeneously and works on a full-measure set of α.
events.remains: All pairs outside that class.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on a measure-theoretic class; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Usuki, ‘On a lower bound of the number of integers in Littlewood’s conjecture’, arXiv 2207.13462 (ID indicates July 2022). Earlier version of the counting result below. Not opened.
events.delivers: Earlier, weaker counting bound for the number of n with small Littlewood product; not read in detail.
events.remains: As for the 2024 improvement.
events.doubts: Not opened; included because the 2024 paper improves it.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Usuki, ‘An improvement of the lower bound of the number of integers in Littlewood’s conjecture’, arXiv 2401.05027 (v1 10 Jan 2024; v2 20 Apr 2024). For γ in (0, 1) and almost all pairs (all except a set of Hausdorff dimension about √γ), the number of n ≤ N with n⟨nα⟩⟨nβ⟩ < ε is at least a universal constant times γ(log N)²/(log log N)², for small ε and large N. First version predates the frozen revision by 16 days.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jan 2024; v2 20 Apr 2024 (39 KB both).
events.delivers: A quantitative lower bound on how many n up to N make the Littlewood product small, for almost all pairs (outside a set of dimension about √γ). Restriction: a counting statement for a large class of pairs, not an all-pairs liminf statement.
events.remains: The liminf-zero statement for every pair, and the exceptional set of pairs.
events.doubts: Scope call: the counted quantity is the Littlewood product itself, but the bound holds only for almost all pairs. The later pass should decide whether this moves the named quantity or counts instances for a class. Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: de Mathan, ‘Simultaneous Diophantine approximation with a divisibility condition’, arXiv 2402.08850 (v1 13 Feb 2024), J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 36 (2024) 987–1008 (per a search summary). Abstract: an earlier paper on sequences of simultaneous rational approximations in R² gave results ‘around the Littlewood conjecture’; ‘such results also hold when we add divisibility conditions’. Its condition (L), as summarised, is the conjecture’s form ‘for every ε > 0 there is (q, r, s) with q > 0 and q|qα − r||qβ − s| ≤ ε’.
events.revisions: v1 13 Feb 2024; published JTNB 36 (2024).
events.delivers: Results near the conjecture’s form (L), with divisibility conditions added. Restriction: divisibility-restricted approximations; the paper does not claim (L) for all pairs.
events.remains: Condition (L) for all pairs, and the conjecture.

checked_by.who: Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux

events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only, so the exact statement of the divisibility-restricted results was not checked.
events.direction: Variant with extra divisibility hypotheses; consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Garrett and Robertson, ‘Counterexamples to the p(t)-adic Littlewood Conjecture over small finite fields’, arXiv 2405.14454 (v1 23 May 2024; v2 8 Apr 2025), later listed as Math. Comp. (2026). Gives an explicit counterexample to the function-field p(t)-adic Littlewood conjecture in characteristic 5, conjectures it for all characteristics p ≡ 1 mod 4, and shows the Adiceam–Nesharim–Lunnon characteristic-3 counterexample also works in characteristics 7 and 11. Computer-assisted, using the authors’ own Python algorithm.
events.revisions: v1 23 May 2024; v2 8 Apr 2025; journal listed as Math. Comp. (2026) in the Wikipedia reference list.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the function-field analogue (characteristic 5), plus the characteristic 7 and 11 extensions. Restriction: function fields over finite fields. The abstract says the work says nothing about the real classical conjecture.
events.remains: The real two-number conjecture, which is the bullet’s subject.
events.directly_checkable: The Laurent series can be checked by computing its continued fraction expansions over F_5; the algorithm is in the paper (not read).
events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Cuts against the function-field analogue only; no bearing on the real conjecture.
events.object: An explicit Laurent series over F_5 that disproves the p(t)-adic Littlewood conjecture in characteristic 5 (the series is in the paper and was not read). Explicit, and computer-assisted rather than AI-assisted.

events.what_happened: Stefanescu, ‘The dispersion of dilated lacunary sequences, with applications in multiplicative Diophantine approximation’, arXiv 2406.19802 (v1 28 Jun 2024), Adv. Math. (2025, per the Wikipedia reference list). For Lebesgue-almost-all α, the maximal gap of the dilates {a_n α} mod 1 is at most (log N)^(2+ε)/N for a Hadamard lacunary sequence. The abstract says this improves Chow and Technau and gives an improved upper bound in the inhomogeneous Littlewood problem.
events.revisions: v1 28 Jun 2024; journal listed as Adv. Math. (2025) in the Wikipedia reference list.
events.delivers: A dispersion bound for lacunary dilates and an inhomogeneous Littlewood-type upper bound. Restriction: almost every dilation factor, and the inhomogeneous version.
events.remains: The homogeneous conjecture for all pairs.
events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Inhomogeneous variant; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Seuret (CNRS seminar, indico event 11072) and Adiceam (Manchester Dynamical Systems and Analysis seminar), talks describing joint work in progress: a family B(σ), σ in [0, 1], interpolating between the badly approximable vectors (B(1)) and the putative counterexamples to the conjecture (B(0)); claimed result that every B(σ) has Hausdorff dimension 2, via a generalised Cantor set built on Ostrowski numeration. No preprint found; not opened (search snippets of the seminar pages only).
events.delivers: Claimed (talk abstracts only) dimension-2 result for the interpolating family B(σ). It is a statement about a set containing the putative counterexamples, not a statement that counterexamples exist or do not exist. Dimension 2 for B(0) does not contradict the dimension-zero result (EKL 2006), since B(0) is a superset of the counterexamples.
events.remains: Whether any counterexample exists; the conjecture itself.
events.doubts: Talk abstracts only; work in progress; dates and results from search snippets; no written argument found.
events.direction: Not a statement either way about the conjecture; a dimension result on a family containing the putative counterexamples.

events.what_happened: Hofer, ‘Variants of the Littlewood conjecture, their connection to uniformly distributed sequences, and the exact order of the discrepancy of van der Corput–Kronecker-type sequences’, arXiv 2501.11362 (v1 20 Jan 2025; v2 29 Aug 2025). Examines Littlewood variants in relation to uniform distribution and determines the exact discrepancy order for van der Corput–Kronecker-type sequences built from X-adic counterexamples over a finite field.
events.delivers: Discrepancy order for sequences built from function-field counterexamples, and discussion of variants. Restriction: discrepancy and function-field variants.
events.remains: All of the real two-number conjecture.
events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Analogue and variant; no bearing on the real conjecture.

events.what_happened: Badziahin, ‘Estimating lower limit in the p-adic Littlewood conjecture’, arXiv 2506.16860 (v1 20 Jun 2025, the only version). For every real x, small primes p, and relatively small ε, the lower limit of q·|q|_p·‖qx‖ is below ε. Explicit: p = 2 with ε = 1/25; for 3 ≤ p ≤ 29, ε at most 1/10. The abstract says this supports the p-adic conjecture, which states the lower limit is 0.
events.revisions: v1 20 Jun 2025 only.
events.delivers: Upper bounds on the p-adic lower limit for p = 2 (ε = 1/25) and 3 ≤ p ≤ 29 (ε ≤ 1/10). Restriction: the p-adic variant and the listed primes; not the real two-number conjecture.
events.remains: The p-adic conjecture for all p and all real x; the real conjecture.
events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only; a computer-verified bound (the abstract mentions computational evidence).
events.direction: Consistent with the p-adic conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Vitorino and Vukusic, ‘Some bounds related to the 2-adic Littlewood conjecture’, arXiv 2506.04110 (June 2025). Per a search summary: the lower bound on the constant C that any 2-adic (bounded partial quotient) counterexample needs rises from 8 (Badziahin) to 15; a limsup ‘B-variant’ gives C ≥ 5. Not opened.
events.delivers: A lower bound of 15 on C for the 2-adic version; a B-variant bound of 5. Restriction: 2-adic, partial-quotient formulation.
events.remains: The 2-adic conjecture and the real conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened; numbers from a search summary.
events.direction: Analogue; no bearing on the real conjecture.

events.what_happened: Robertson, ‘Combinatorics on number walls and the p(t)-adic Littlewood conjecture’, arXiv 2307.00955 (v1 about July 2023), listed as Mathematika (2026) in the Wikipedia reference list. Function-field combinatorics. Not opened; content not read.
events.revisions: v1 about July 2023 (from arXiv identifier); journal Mathematika (2026) per Wikipedia.
events.delivers: Function-field combinatorial results on the p(t)-adic conjecture. Content not read.
events.remains: The real two-number conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened.
events.direction: Analogue; no bearing on the real conjecture.

events.what_happened: Schleischitz, ‘Disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture’, arXiv 2603.12611 (v1 13 Mar 2026, the only version). Disproves the uniform Littlewood conjecture (ULC) of Bandi, Fregoli and Kleinbock: for a sup over pairs, the limsup of Q·min over 1 ≤ q ≤ Q of ‖qξ‖‖qζ‖ is positive (the abstract gives 0.005326 as a lower value for the sup). Counterexamples form a residual set; a mildly twisted version has dimension at least 1; also disproves uniform p-adic and twisted S-arithmetic variants. The disproof is semi-constructive: the non-constructive part uses effective results on Zaremba’s conjecture (Bourgain–Kontorovich) and product-set estimates over finite fields.
events.revisions: v1 13 Mar 2026 only (arXiv abstract page lists no later version).
events.delivers: The uniform (all-scales, for every Q) statement is false. Restriction: the uniform variant. The paper says its counterexamples do not disprove the classical conjecture: both numbers have irrationality exponent at least 3, so they are not badly approximable, while classical counterexamples must be badly approximable.
events.remains: The classical liminf statement, which the paper states it does not address. Whether uniform failure can occur with bounded partial quotients was left open, per a later paper.

checked_by.qualification: Diophantine approximation specialist; co-author of the Bugeaud–Moshchevitin results cited above.
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a simpler, Fibonacci-based proof of a counterexample to the ULC (arXiv 2605.26188, 25 May 2026). A digested rewrite, not a referee report.

events.directly_checkable: The counterexample pairs are explicit in Moshchevitin’s note (Fibonacci construction); Schleischitz’s general construction is semi-constructive.
events.doubts: No substantive doubt found in the sources I read. The constant for the sup (0.005326) differs from the constant quoted for the Fibonacci pair in Moshchevitin’s note (≈0.381966); a search summary attributed 0.005326 to Schleischitz’s original; I could not reconcile these and it does not change the status.
events.direction: Cuts against the uniform variant; per the paper itself, does not cut against the classical conjecture.
events.object: Pairs (ξ, ζ) with irrationality exponent at least 3 for which the uniform quantity has positive limsup, residually many of them; the disproof combines a semi-constructive construction with a non-constructive step relying on effective Zaremba results and product-set estimates over finite fields. Not a single explicit pair in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Moshchevitin, ‘A note on uniform version of Littlewood inequality and Fibonacci numbers’, arXiv 2605.26188 (v1 25 May 2026). Gives a simple proof of Schleischitz’s counterexample to the ULC, using simple properties of Fibonacci numbers. For the constructed α, β the limsup of Q·min over 1 ≤ x < Q of ‖αx‖‖βx‖ is at least 2/(3+√5) ≈ 0.381966. Acknowledgements thank Shulga and Schleischitz for discussion.
events.revisions: v1 25 May 2026 only.
events.delivers: An explicit, elementary counterexample pair to the uniform conjecture (limsup ≥ 0.381966). Restriction: uniform variant only.
events.remains: The classical conjecture (the paper says so).
events.directly_checkable: The Fibonacci-based pair can be checked by hand with the stated estimate.
events.doubts: The constant conflicts with the 0.005326 figure in a search summary; see the Schleischitz entry.
events.direction: Cuts against the uniform variant only.
events.object: An explicit pair (α, β) built from Fibonacci numbers for which the uniform limsup is at least 2/(3+√5) ≈ 0.381966. Explicit.

events.what_happened: Brouckė, Matolcsi and Révész, ‘On a question of Gowers related to Littlewood’s conjecture’, arXiv 2607.27780 (v1 30 Jul 2026; v2 27 Sep 2026, ‘minor changes before journal submission’). Answers a question raised by Gowers in a 2009 blog post about an approach to the conjecture via hyperbolic distances among points of the unit cube, by an explicit construction (a Minkowski-embedded lattice of a totally real number field’s integers meets the hyperbolic region only at 0). They conclude that this approach cannot prove the conjecture unless refinements are added.
events.revisions: v1 30 Jul 2026; v2 27 Sep 2026 (minor changes before journal submission).
events.delivers: Shows that one particular proof strategy (Gowers’s hyperbolic-distance approach, in its stated form) cannot work. Restriction: the method; it does not bear on the truth of the conjecture, and the authors say so.
events.remains: The conjecture as a whole.
events.directly_checkable: The lattice construction can be checked by hand from the paper (not read in detail).
events.direction: Negative result on a proof method; neutral on the conjecture.
events.object: An explicit configuration of points in the unit cube (via the Minkowski embedding of the ring of integers of a totally real number field, a full-rank lattice meeting the hyperbolic region only at 0) with pairwise large hyperbolic distances, answering Gowers’s question. Explicit construction.

events.what_happened: Schleischitz, ‘On an inhomogeneous uniform Littlewood type problem’, arXiv 2607.08114 (v1 9 Jul 2026). Gives a positive answer to a fully inhomogeneous uniform problem: for any θ1, θ2, the set of (ξ, ζ) with positive limsup of Q·min over q of ‖qξ − θ1‖‖qζ − θ2‖ contains a dense G_δ set. States that the three-variable homogeneous analogue may be as hard as the classical problem. Read from the HTML rendering; the summariser reported no acknowledgements section, so the full text was not confirmed.
events.revisions: v1 9 Jul 2026 only (as read).
events.delivers: Uniform, fully inhomogeneous variant: counterexample sets are dense G_δ for every choice of shifts. Restriction: the uniform, inhomogeneous, two-variable setting.
events.remains: The classical homogeneous conjecture, which the paper does not settle.
events.doubts: Read partly from a summary; the statement of Problem 1 and its theorem were read through the summariser.
events.direction: Cuts against the fully inhomogeneous uniform variant; no direct bearing on the classical conjecture.

events.what_happened: Shulga, ‘The uniform Littlewood conjecture fails on a set of positive Hausdorff dimension’, arXiv 2608.25059 (v1 25 Aug 2026, the only version). Shows that counterexamples to the ULC with a badly approximable first coordinate have Hausdorff dimension at least 3/2, and that the badly approximable ξ occurring in some counterexample form a full-dimension set. Contrasts the classical case, where the set of counterexamples has dimension zero. Acknowledges Moshchevitin and Schleischitz.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2026 only.
events.delivers: ULC counterexample set has positive Hausdorff dimension (≥ 3/2 with a badly approximable first coordinate). Restriction: uniform variant.
events.remains: The classical conjecture (the paper uses the dimension-zero result for the classical case only as a contrast).
events.doubts: Not yet checked by a second source I could find. The later preprint 2608.24401 reports full dimension, which is a stronger claim about the same set.
events.direction: Cuts against the uniform variant; the paper itself treats the classical case as separate.
events.object: Pairs (ξ, ζ) with badly approximable ξ forming counterexamples to the ULC, in a set of Hausdorff dimension at least 3/2 (via a Cantor-type construction over continued fractions with bounded partial quotients). Constructive in the sense of an explicit dimension argument.

events.what_happened: Neckrasov, Wu and Yang, ‘Winning property of counterexamples to Uniform Littlewood’s Conjecture’, arXiv 2608.24401 (v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 3 Sep 2026). Shows the set of real pairs that are counterexamples to the ULC is hyperplane absolute winning, hence of full Hausdorff dimension in R²; a liminf-type subset along a sequence Q_m with Q_{m+1} at least a power Q_m^τ, τ > 1, has the same property; absolute winning along certain planar curves. Acknowledgements: ‘During the preparation of this work, the authors used GPT-5.6 Pro to assist in doing calculations and checking proofs. All mathematical arguments were subsequently verified independently by the authors, who take full responsibility for the correctness of the results.’ Read from the HTML rendering through a summariser (the PDF did not decode); the quote is the summariser’s rendering of that page, not my reading of the raw source.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 3 Sep 2026 (v2 is the version read). Whether v1 has the same acknowledgement was not checked.
events.delivers: Full Hausdorff dimension in R² for ULC counterexample sets (a limsup-type set and a liminf-type subset along growing sequences). Restriction: the uniform variant. The paper states that the classical counterexample set E′ (liminf-type) is contained in the uniform set and has Hausdorff dimension zero by EKL, so the classical statement is not affected.
events.remains: The classical conjecture.
events.doubts: Authors say all arguments were verified independently by the authors; no outside check found. The GPT-5.6 Pro role is ambiguous: ‘assist in doing calculations’ does not say which calculations, or whether they enter the main theorem.
events.direction: Cuts against the uniform variant and reaffirms dimension zero for the classical counterexample set.
events.object: A set of planar pairs (x, y) that are counterexamples to the ULC, shown to be hyperplane absolute winning and so of full dimension; a subset along a lacunary sequence has the same property. A set, not an explicit single pair.

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Authors’ words: ‘to assist in doing calculations and checking proofs’. The source does not say which calculations, or whether any feed the main theorem.
systems.basis_quote: During the preparation of this work, the authors used GPT-5.6 Pro to assist in doing calculations and checking proofs.

events.what_happened: Per the Wikipedia article (last edited 5 Oct 2026): in 2026 Matala-Aho, Törmä and Vapa introduced an algorithm, based on simple continued-fraction expansions of α and β, for checking proposed universal upper bounds on m_LC, and used it to obtain a further universal estimate. The reference list gives ‘Numerical upper bounds in the Littlewood conjecture’, Experimental Mathematics (2026). I could not locate the paper on arXiv or in search, so its date, bound and method are unverified.
events.delivers: Unverified: per Wikipedia, a further universal upper bound on m_LC. If so, it bounds the supremum that the conjecture equates with 0, moving the named quantity without settling it. The value is not known to me.
events.remains: m_LC = 0, i.e. the conjecture.
events.doubts: The paper was not located, so the bound, its date and any checking are unknown.
events.direction: If it is an upper bound on m_LC: consistent with the conjecture, a bound on the named quantity; cannot establish 0.

events.what_happened: Bloom and Green, ‘Remarks on the inverse Littlewood conjecture’, arXiv 2602.16482 (v1 18 Feb 2026; v2 18 Apr 2026). A different problem sharing a name: the L1 norm of the Fourier transform of a finite integer set, where the classical result (Konyagin; McGehee–Pigno–Smith, 1980s) gives a lower bound. The paper asks what structure a set must have when the norm is at most K·log N, and shows additive structure (small doubling, arithmetic progressions).
events.delivers: Results on a different (inverse, additive-combinatorial) Littlewood problem. Restriction: not about Diophantine approximation; settles nothing here.
events.remains: All of this bullet.
events.doubts: Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Not about this problem; a namesake.

summary: Nothing I found shows the classical conjecture resolved, a case of it settled, or its status changed since 26 January 2024. The Wikipedia article (last edited 5 Oct 2026) still calls it unresolved, and no search turned up a claimed proof or counterexample, AI-assisted or otherwise. The in-window activity bears on neighbouring problems. (i) The uniform variant of Bandi, Fregoli and Kleinbock was disproved by Schleischitz (arXiv 2603.12611, 13 Mar 2026), with a simpler Fibonacci proof by Moshchevitin (25 May 2026), a fully inhomogeneous version by Schleischitz (9 Jul 2026), and positive-dimension results by Shulga and by Neckrasov, Wu and Yang (both 25 Aug 2026). Each of these says, or the text shows, that the classical statement is not touched: the uniform counterexamples have irrationality exponent at least 3 and so are not badly approximable, whereas classical counterexamples must be, and classical counterexamples form a dimension-zero set (EKL 2006). (ii) Analogues and variants: p-adic (Badziahin 2025), 2-adic (Vitorino and Vukusic 2025), function-field p(t)-adic (Garrett and Robertson 2024), and a divisibility-restricted variant (de Mathan 2024). (iii) Almost-every-pair and inhomogeneous partial results: Usuki’s counting bound, first posted 10 Jan 2024, which predates the freeze by sixteen days and so is recorded as predating it; Chow and Technau (2023); Stefanescu (2024). (iv) Broucke, Matolcsi and Révész (30 Jul 2026) show that Gowers’s 2009 hyperbolic-distance approach cannot prove the conjecture unless refined; they say no AI tools were used. The only AI involvement I found on this problem is the acknowledgement in Neckrasov, Wu and Yang: ‘the authors used GPT-5.6 Pro to assist in doing calculations and checking proofs’. That is on the uniform variant, and it is ambiguous: checking proofs is not the kind of contribution the protocol counts, but calculations could be load-bearing, and the authors do not say which calculations enter the main theorem. I list it as a system with the literal quote and leave the call to the later pass. No AI system is credited with anything on the classical problem. Close calls. (a) The 2026 Matala-Aho, Törmä and Vapa paper in Experimental Mathematics, which Wikipedia says gives a further universal upper bound on m_LC. Since the conjecture is equivalent to m_LC = 0, a bound on m_LC moves the named quantity without settling it. I could not locate the paper, so its date, value and method are unverified; that is the only in-window event that touches the named quantity. (b) Usuki’s count: the product being counted is the conjecture’s own quantity, but the bound holds only for almost all pairs. (c) Schleischitz’s disproof: a failure of the stronger uniform statement does not disprove the classical one, and the paper says so. (d) Numbers: Moshchevitin’s note states ≈0.381966 for its Fibonacci pair, while a search summary attributes 0.005326 to Schleischitz’s original; I could not reconcile these, and they do not change the status. Scope: I read the abstract pages of most pre-2026 items and the full HTML of the uniform-variant papers, so the AI statements in the older items rest on abstracts.
competing_reading: A reader could treat the Schleischitz, Moshchevitin, Shulga, Neckrasov, Wu and Yang sequence as the most significant in-window progress in the Littlewood family, since the uniform conjecture is the natural sharpening and its disproof is a large step; on that view the GPT-5.6 Pro sentence is the first AI-assisted development in the family, and the event counts. Against this, every paper in the sequence states or implies that the classical case is unaffected, and the AI sentence speaks of calculations and proof-checking, not of an idea the proof turns on. A second reading treats the unlocated Matala-Aho bound as a bound on the named quantity m_LC and so as in-window progress on the statement itself; the opposing reading treats it as a numerical bound on an auxiliary constant that does not answer the bullet’s question.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Matala-Aho, Törmä and Vapa paper in Experimental Mathematics: its date, the bound it proves on m_LC, and whether that bound is on the supremum the conjecture sets to zero. (2) The raw PDF or TeX source of arXiv 2608.24401 (v1 and v2): whether the GPT-5.6 Pro sentence appears verbatim, which calculations it refers to, and whether those calculations are used in the main theorem’s proof. (3) The definition and scope sentences in arXiv 2603.12611 and 2608.25059 read from the PDF, to confirm that the classical conjecture is not affected, since the PDF fetches failed and I relied on HTML renderings.

No Lean, Mathlib or formal-proof record for the Littlewood conjecture was found. A DeepMind formal_conjectures dependency listing came up, but I did not check its repository for this entry.

No Erdős-problems or AI-tracker entry for this problem was found; the conjecture is not one of Erdős’s problems, and the Erdős AI tracker is about other problems.

incomplete: (1) The Matala-Aho, Törmä and Vapa 2026 paper on numerical upper bounds for m_LC was not located. Its date, bound and method are unverified, and it may be the only in-window event on the named quantity. (2) Several pre-2024 primary sources were read only through Wikipedia, search summaries, or the abstract page: Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer (1955), Gallagher (1962), Shapira (2011), Bugeaud–Moshchevitin (2009), Pollington–Velani (2000), Usuki (2022), Badziahin (2016, via the Durham record), Robertson (2023), Chow–Yang (2019), Chow–Zafeiropoulos (2021), Vitorino–Vukusic (2025). Their full texts and AI statements were not read. (3) The PDFs of arXiv 2608.24401, 2603.12611, 2608.25059 and 2607.08114 did not decode through the fetch tool. Their acknowledgements and AI statements were checked only in arXiv HTML renderings passed through a summariser. The GPT-5.6 Pro quotation is therefore a rendering of the authors’ text, not my reading of the raw source; the v1 text of 2608.24401 was not checked. (4) The Schleischitz 2607.08114 HTML summary said there was no acknowledgements section; that was not confirmed in the raw text. (5) The Adiceam–Seuret result and the original Bandi–Fregoli–Kleinbock paper introducing the uniform conjecture were not located. Math. 2025) come from the Wikipedia reference list and were not verified at the publishers.
